answer.rationale: The mandate demands an 18% cut, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone would satisfy it, but the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer and only 14 days to contract expiry — a full vendor switch under that timeline risks delivery interruption based on a single prior onboarding data point (memory_c2), which said nothing about performance under a tight cutover with no slack. Memory_c4 shows that benchmarking against market rates (which now includes the low-cost quote) has previously moved the incumbent on both price and terms without any migration risk, and memory_c1/c6 confirm the incumbent relationship has stayed stable and can support volume-based cost reductions without narrowing scope. Given only one sourcing action is available this cycle, negotiating with the incumbent using the low-cost quote as leverage is the path most likely to meet the cost mandate while holding delivery risk flat; if it fails to close the full 18% gap, switching or second-sourcing remains available next cycle. I verified c4 and c2 because they are the two memories most directly in tension for this decision — one supports leverage-based negotiation, the other supports outright switching — and confirming their original records is necessary before betting the only decision slot this cycle on interpreting them correctly.
